title: Corn at the drugstore
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: A crate of corn by the drugstore's door. Late August. The strip's month coming. Wood buys four ears and doesn't say why. The clerk says corn or peas. Wood says how does he know that. The clerk says the digest, three years ago. The clerk reads.

panels.composition: The drugstore's door. A crate of corn in husks on the sidewalk. WOOD picking four. BARNABY sniffing the crate.

image.prompt: a crate of husked corn on a sidewalk outside a drugstore with a young man choosing four ears and a small dog sniffing the crate, black and white, no words
a drugstore clerk at a register, dry, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood, holding four ears. The clerk reads. Everyone reads.

image.prompt: a young man at a register holding four ears of corn, taken aback, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood on the sidewalk with the corn under his arm. September in two days. The strip's month. The clerk's been reading since the Timberline.
